title: Finite separable top extensions preserve nonalgebraic separability
statement: Let $k\subseteq L\subseteq M$ be a tower of fields [def-pc-field-extension]. Suppose that $L/k$ is separable in the possibly transcendental sense [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]: every intermediate field $k\subseteq L_0\subseteq L$ finitely generated as a field over $k$ is separably generated over $k$. Suppose that $M/L$ is finite separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Then $M/k$ is separable in the same possibly transcendental sense. Finite means finite-dimensional; no algebraicity or finite generation of $L/k$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BRM, lemma-abhyankar, final paragraph: the finite separable extension of kappa_B is separable over kappa_A; the nonalgebraic notion is Algebra Tag 030O (definition-separable-field-extension), with Tag 030X (lemma-separably-generated-separable).

proof.text: If $\operatorname{char}(k)=0$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-separable] to $M/k$ and finish. Otherwise $\operatorname{char}(k)=p$ for a prime $p$. Fix any field extension $E/k$. Give all tensor products below their commutative algebra structures using [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Put $S=L\otimes_k E$, with $L$-algebra map $\ell\mapsto\ell\otimes1$. We will show $M\otimes_kE$ is reduced for every such $E$.

First $S$ is reduced. For a nilpotent $z\in S$, write $z=\sum_{i=1}^r\ell_i\otimes e_i$, possible because pure tensors generate [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Set $F=k(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r)\subseteq L$. This is a finitely generated intermediate field, so the hypothesis on $L/k$ and [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension] make $F/k$ separably generated. Since $E$ is a field, it is reduced; hence [lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-tensor-reduced] makes $F\otimes_k E$ reduced. The inclusion $F\hookrightarrow L$ remains injective after tensoring with $E$: use [lem-weil-pbc-module-over-field-flat] and [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection], with the elementary interchange $x\otimes y\leftrightarrow y\otimes x$ if necessary. Its tensor map $j:F\otimes_kE\to S$ is also a ring map, as multiplication on pure tensors shows. For $y=\sum_i\ell_i\otimes e_i$ in its source, $j(y)=z$. If $z^n=0$ with $n>0$, then $j(y^n)=0$, injectivity gives $y^n=0$, reducedness gives $y=0$, and thus $z=0$.

source.place: Tag 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness), finite-subextension reduction; the finite-coefficient and injectivity argument is written explicitly

proof.text: The empty family is a transcendence basis of $M/L$: it is algebraically independent because the associated polynomial evaluation is the injective field map $L\hookrightarrow M$, and $M/L$ is algebraic by hypothesis. Its generated subfield is $L$. By [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis], [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], and clause (1) of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension], the given separability of $M/L$ therefore makes $M/L$ separably generated. This uses no finite generation of $L/k$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separably-generated-tensor-reduced] over the field $L$ to the separably generated extension $M/L$ and the reduced $L$-algebra $S$ from step 2. It gives reducedness of $M\otimes_L(L\otimes_k E)$. The elementary ring isomorphism to $M\otimes_k E$ sends $m\otimes(\ell\otimes e)$ to $m\ell\otimes e$, with inverse $m\otimes e\mapsto m\otimes(1\otimes e)$. These maps are additive and multiplicative by the pure-tensor formulas. Balancing over $L$ identifies $m\ell\otimes(1\otimes e)$ with $m\otimes(\ell\otimes e)$; balancing over $k$ identifies $ma\otimes(1\otimes e)$ with $m\otimes(1\otimes ae)$ for $a\in k$. Thus both formulas descend, and their composites are the identity on pure tensors, hence everywhere by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. A nilpotent maps under the inverse to a nilpotent in the reduced source and is zero. Consequently $M\otimes_k E$ is reduced.

source.place: Tag 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness); explicit tensor reassociation for the tower

proof.text: The extension $E/k$ was arbitrary. In characteristic $p>0$, [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-reduced-extension-separable] applied to $M/k$ and the reducedness proved in step 4 says that every finitely generated intermediate field of $M/k$ is separably generated. This is exactly the required separability. Together with step 1 this covers every characteristic.
